overview.title: Index: I to L (intelligent agents to LayoutMap)

overview.central_idea: This page finishes I, then covers J (JAX), K (Keras and its many sub-entries, KerasHub, KerasTuner, K-fold validation) and the start of L (L1/L2 regularization, language models, latent space, layers).
overview.importance: The Keras and JAX entries map the book's framework material, and the language-models entry maps its NLP chapters.

summary:
Index page printed 614 (PDF 638). Locators are **printed** pages: **add 24** for the PDF page.

**I (end).** *intelligent agents* 571. *intermediate activations, visualizing* 285–291 (PDF 309–315). *interpolation* 145, 463 (PDF 169). *IoU (Intersection over Union)* 316, 343 (PDF 340, 367).

**J.** *JAX*: class activation heatmap 303, customizing fit() 225, gradient ascent 295, relationship between frameworks 63 (PDF 87), training step functions 218 (PDF 242), train_step() metrics 228, model parallelism 552 (PDF 576). *jax.debug.visualize_sharding* 555. *Jupyter notebook* 17 (PDF 41).

**K.** *Kaggle* 607. *kagglehub* 242, 485. *kaleidoscope hypothesis* 577 (PDF 601). **Keras** 60, 190 (PDF 84, 214), with sub-entries: building models 192, Functional API 195–200, implementing VAEs 513–518 (PDF 537–542), training loops 206–214 (PDF 230–238), training step functions 216–218, Sequential model 192, subclassing Model 202, using the right tool for the job 205. *Keras API, recurrent layers in* 368–372 (PDF 392–396). *keras.callbacks*, *keras.metrics*. *KerasHub* 258, 300 (PDF 282). *KerasTuner* 540–546 (PDF 564–570). *K-fold validation* 129–134, 151 (PDF 153–158, 175). *K-means* 585.

**L.** *L1/L2 regularization* 165 (PDF 189). *labels* 105, 214. **language models** 421–428 (PDF 445–452), with sub-entries: classification with a pretrained Transformer 454–461, dot-product attention 439, generating Shakespeare 426–428, seq2seq learning 428–437 (PDF 452–461), Transformer 444, 447, 462–464 and Transformer architecture 437 (PDF 461). *latent space* 509, 568 (PDF 533, 592), of text-to-image models 533–537. *LayerNormalization* 445 (PDF 469). *layers* 596. *LayoutMap API* 553–555.

concepts.name: Keras (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 60, 190 (PDF 84, 214). Sub-entries cover building models (192), the Functional API (195–200), training loops (206–214) and training step functions (216–218).
concepts.intuition: PDF 214–254 is the core 'working with Keras' material.
concepts.technical: 'relationship between frameworks 63' (PDF 87) explains how Keras sits on top of JAX, TensorFlow and PyTorch.
concepts.significance: Every code example in the book uses Keras.
concepts.example: Open PDF 240 for training step functions.
concepts.misconception: Keras is not tied to TensorFlow. The book uses it with multiple backends.

concepts.name: language models (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 421–428 (PDF 445–452). Sub-entries: seq2seq 428–437, Transformer 444–464, classification with a pretrained Transformer 454–461.
concepts.intuition: The book starts with a character-level Shakespeare model and builds up to Transformers.
concepts.technical: Related entries: LLMs 468 and mini-GPT 470–484 are on the next index page.
concepts.significance: Language models are the foundation of modern NLP and of LLMs.
concepts.misconception: Language modeling and text classification are different tasks, even when they use the same architecture.

concepts.name: K-fold validation (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 129–134, 151 (PDF 153–158, 175); iterated with shuffling at 152.
concepts.intuition: PDF 153 uses it in the housing-price regression example, and PDF 175 sets out the general protocol.
concepts.technical: It is used when the dataset is too small for a single hold-out split.
concepts.significance: It gives a reliable evaluation on small data.
concepts.misconception: K-fold does not replace a final test set.
